statement.p: Find f if \nabla f=8xy\,\vec i+(4x^{2}+9y^{2})\,\vec j

static.solution: \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} = 8xy\quad\hbox{and}\quad \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = 4x^{2}+9y^{2}. Now think of y as a constant in the equation for \partial f/\partial x and integrate, giving f(x,y) = 4 x^2y + C(y). Since the constant of integration may depend on y, it is written C(y). Differentiating this expression for f(x,y) with respect to y and using the fact that \partial f/\partial y = 4x^{2}+9y^{2}, we get \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = 4 x^2 + C'(y) = 4x^{2}+9y^{2}. Therefore C'(y) = 9 y^{2}\quad\hbox{so}\quad C(y)=3 y^{3} + K. for some constant K. Thus, f(x,y) = 4x^{2}y+3y^{3}+K.
